label: def:pack-non-simple
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:pack-non-simple}
   Let $T$ is a disk, sphere or infinite plane triangulation with  multiple edges. If $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is empty, then we set the circle packing for $T$ to be empty. If $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is not empty, we define circle packings for $T$ as below. Let $\widetilde\mathcal{P} = \{\widetilde D_v:v\in \mathcal{V}\Phi_{\rm simple}(T) \}$ be a circle packing for $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$. For a vertex $v\in\mathcal{V} T$, if $v\in \mathcal{V}\Phi_{\rm simple}(T) $, then we let $D_v = \widetilde D_v$. If $v\notin \mathcal{V}\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$, let $(v_1,v_2)\in \mathcal{V}\Phi_{\rm simple}(T) $  be the unique pair of vertices such that the vertex $v$ is removed when we collapse multiple edges between $v_1$ and $v_2$. Then we let $D_v$ be the tangent point between the disks $D_{v_1}$ and $D_{v_2}$, and we view $D_v$ as a degenerate disk. We call $\mathcal{P}:=\{D_v:v\in\mathcal{V} T\}$ a circle packing for $T$. If $T$ is an infinite triangulation, we say $T$ is circle packing parabolic (resp.\ hyperbolic) if $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is circle packing parabolic (resp.\ hyperbolic).

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:hat}
    Let $J=[t_J^-,t_J^+]$ be a finite interval. Suppose $\mathring\mathcal{J}\cap J=\emptyset$. Then there exists $t^-<t^+$ such that $J\subseteq [t^-,t^+]$ and~\eqref{eq:double-edge-Mullin-A} holds.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We say a finite interval $[t^-,t^+]$ is bad if  ~\eqref{eq:double-edge-Mullin-A} holds (where $t^-,t^+$ are not necessarily in $\mathcal{J}$). Observe that if $I_1,I_2$ are bad and $I_1\cap I_2\neq\emptyset$, then $I_1\cup I_2$ is also bad. If $J\cap\mathcal{J}=\emptyset$, then $\mathcal{Z}$ is constant over $J$ and the conclusion holds. Otherwise, let $t_1,...,t_p = J\cap\mathcal{J}$. Then for each $j=1,...,p$, $t_j\notin \mathring\mathcal{J}$ and therefore there exists $t_j^-<t_j\leq t_j^+$ such that~\eqref{eq:double-edge-Mullin-A} holds for $(t^-,t^+)=(t_j^-,t_j^+)$. Since the walk is constant between times in $\mathcal{J}$, we may further assume that $t_J^-\geq t_1^-$ and $t_j^-\leq t_{j-1}$ for $j\geq 2$. Then $\cup_{j=1}^p[t_j^-,t_j^+]$ is a bad interval covering $[t_J^-,t_p]$, and since $\mathcal{Z}$ is constant over $[t_p,t_J^+]$, $[t_p,t_J^+]$ is also a bad interval. Therefore  $[t_p,t_J^+]\cup(\bigcup_{j=1}^p[t_j^-,t_j^+])$ is a bad interval covering $J$, which finishes the proof.

title: Proof

body_md:
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-excursion}, a union bound and translation invariance, for the simple random walk $(\mathcal{X}_n,\mathcal{Y}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-gam-hat-J-Q}\mathbb{P}\big[\exists i_1\leq -n, i_2\geq0, s.t., \mathcal{X}_{i_1}=\mathcal{X}_{i_2}=\inf_{i_1\leq j\leq i_2}\mathcal{X}_i,\mathcal{Y}_{i_1}=\mathcal{Y}_{i_2}=\inf_{i_1\leq j\leq i_2}\mathcal{Y}_i\big]\leq cn^{-1}.\end{equation}
Now for $i\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $J_i = [2^{\alpha m-1}i,2^{\alpha m-1}(i+1)]$. Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,2-1/\alpha)$. By part~(\ref{cond:prop:KMT-gamma-cone-(i)}) of Theorem~\ref{prop:KMT-gamma-cone},  $\mathcal{J}$ is a Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}$, and  $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{Q}[\#(J_i\cap \mathcal{J})\leq 2^{(1-\varepsilon)\alpha m}]\leq c2^{-c_\varepsilon m^2}$.    Then by Lemma~\ref{lem:hat}, ~\eqref{eq:pf-gam-hat-J-Q} and translation invariance for the random walk $(\mathcal{X}_n,\mathcal{Y}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$, one can check using part~(\ref{cond:prop:KMT-gamma-cone-(i)}) of Theorem~\ref{prop:KMT-gamma-cone} that $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{Q}\big[J_i\cap\mathring\mathcal{J}=\emptyset\big]\leq c2^{-(1-\varepsilon)\alpha m}$. By a further union bound over $J_i$, we have
$$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{Q}\big[J_i\cap\mathring\mathcal{J}=\emptyset,\  \ \text{for some } i \in[ -2^{(1-\alpha)m+1}-2,2^{(1-\alpha)m+1}+2]\cap\mathbb{Z} \big]\lesssim 2^{(1-(2-\varepsilon)\alpha)m},$$
which further implies~\eqref{eq:lem:gap-hat-J-Q} since every $J\subseteq [-2^m,2^m]$ with $ |J|=2^{\alpha m}$ contains some $J_i$ for $ i \in[ -2^{(1-\alpha)m+1}-2,2^{(1-\alpha)m+1}+2]\cap\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Proof

    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[B(0;2^{-\theta n})\nsubseteq\eta([-2^{-(\theta-\delta)n/\gamma Q},2^{-(\theta-\delta)n/\gamma Q}  ]) ]\lesssim  2^{-c_3''n}; \ \ \ \mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\eta([-2^{-\varepsilon_2n},2^{-\varepsilon_2n}])\nsubseteq \mathbb{D}]\lesssim  2^{-c_3''n}. $$}
    Pick $\theta,\delta,\varepsilon_2<\varepsilon_1$ such that $\varepsilon_3:=(\theta-\delta)/\gamma Q>\varepsilon_2$ and $\varepsilon_4:=\beta-\frac{\gamma^2\theta}{2}+\frac{\varepsilon_2}{2}>0$.
    We reparameterize $\mathring\eta$ by the quantum area to transfer back to $\eta$. By a union bound, for some constant $c_5',c_5''>0$, under the probability measure $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}$, with probability at least $1-c_5'2^{-c_5''n}$, for any $t^-<t^+$ where $t^-,t^+\in [-2^{-\varepsilon_2n},2^{-\varepsilon_2n}]\backslash [-2^{-\varepsilon_3 n},2^{-\varepsilon_3 n}  ]$ with $t^+-t^-> 2^{-\varepsilon_1n}$, we have $\nu_h(\partial \eta([t^-,t^+]))\geq 2^{(\beta-\frac{1+\gamma^2\theta}{2})n}$. title: Proof
body_md:
We only deal with the $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$ case as the proof for $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}$ is identical.  The boundary length process for $(h(C\cdot+z)+Q\log C, h^\mathrm{IG}(C\cdot+z))$ is $(Z_{t+\tau_z}-Z_{\tau_z})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ and by relation~\eqref{eq:shift-inv-Z} as in part~(\ref{cond:thm:KMT-0-cone-(i)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:KMT-0-cone}, the corresponding discrete-time walk for $(h(C\cdot+z)+Q\log C, h^\mathrm{IG}(C\cdot+z) ,\mathfrak{U}-\tau_z)$ is $(\mathcal{Z}_{t+\tau_z}-\mathcal{Z}_{\tau_z})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$.  The relation~\eqref{eq:lem:ergodicity-200} is a consequence of the fact that the time sets are invariant if we add a constant to the walk $\mathcal{Z}$ and our construction of the cells commutes with translation and scaling. 

Now let $\mathcal{F}_n = \sigma(h|_{B(0;n)}, h^\mathrm{IG}|_{B(0;n)}, \mathfrak{U},\mathfrak{D}^\mathbb{C})$. Let $S_j\in\mathfrak{D}^\mathbb{C}$ be the a.s.\ unique square containing 0 of side length within $[2^j,2^{j+1})$. Then there exists a finite integer $K_m$ which is measurable with respect to $\sigma(h,h^\mathrm{IG},\mathfrak{U},\mathfrak{D}^\mathbb{C})$ such that $\widehat S_m = S_{K_m}$. For each integer $j$, let $p_{n,j} = \mathbb{E}[\mathds{1}_{K_m=j}|\mathcal{F}_n]$. Then by the martingale convergence theorem, almost surely, for each $j$, $p_{n,j}\to \mathds{1}_{K_m=j}$. Let $K_{m,n} = j$ if $p_{n,j}>2/3$ for some $j$ and $K_{m,n}=0$ otherwise. Since $\sum_j p_{n,j} = 1$, there is at most one $j$ such that $p_{n,j}>2/3$ so $K_{m,n}$ is well-defined and measurable with respect to $\mathcal{F}_n$. Therefore combined with $p_{n,j}\to \mathds{1}_{K_m=j}$, almost surely, for all sufficiently large $n$, $K_{m,n}=K_m$. Therefore the claim~\eqref{eq:lem:ergodicity-200201} holds if we set $\psi_{m,n}(h|_{B(0;n)},h^{\mathrm{IG}}|_{B(0;n)},\mathfrak{U},\mathfrak{D}^\mathbb{C}) = S_{K_{m,n}}$. The proof for $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}$ is identical.

body_md:
We only prove the claim for $(\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell},\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large})$ as the proof for the other one  {follows from the same argument as in \cite[Lemma 5.26]{Tutte}}. Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$.  By Proposition~ef{prop:moment-bound-1} and Lemma~ef{lem:GMS2.9}, where we set the conductance to be equal to 1 for all the edges in $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}$,   almost surely for large enough $r>1$, for all $H\in\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}([-r,r]^2)$  and $H\in\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}([-r,r]^2)$ we have $\mathrm{diam}(H)\leq \varepsilon r/3$. In particular, by~\eqref{eq:cell-area}, for all $s\in\mathring\mathcal{J}^-$ such that $\eta(\mathring I_s)\cap [-r,r]^2
eq\emptyset$ we have $\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))\leq \varepsilon r/3$.

   Let $\ell\subseteq B(0;r)$  with length at least $\varepsilon r$, and suppose $\mathring H_{t}^\mathrm{cell}\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$ and $\mathring H_{t'}^\mathrm{cell}\cap \ell
eq \emptyset$. Below we assume $r$ is sufficiently large. Then  $\ell$ intersects the outer boundaries of $\mathring H_{t}^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring H_{t'}^\mathrm{cell}$ and therefore $\ell\cap \mathring H_{t}^\mathrm{large}
eq\emptyset$ and  $\ell\cap \mathring H_{t'}^\mathrm{large}
eq\emptyset$ by our construction. From our definition of $\mathring H_t^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring H_{t'}^\mathrm{cell}$, there exists $s\in  \mathring\mathcal{T}_t^\mathrm{cell}=\mathring\mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $s'\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{t'}^\mathrm{cell}=\mathring\mathcal{T}_{t'}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ such that $\eta(\mathring I_s)\cap \ell
eq\emptyset$ and $\eta(\mathring I_{s'})\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$. Then $\partial\eta(\mathring I_s)\cap \ell
eq\emptyset$ and $\partial\eta(\mathring I_{s'})\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$.  Using the line connectivity property for $\{\eta(\mathring I_s):s\in\mathcal{J}^-\}$ as similar in the proof of~\cite[Proposition 3.1]{GMS21tutte}, one can find $s_1,...,s_n\in \mathring\mathcal{J}^-$ such that $s_1=s$ and $s_n=s'$, and for $j=1,...,n-1$, $\{s_j,s_{j+1}\}\in\mathring\mathcal{E}_\mathrm{G}$ and $\eta(\mathring I_{s_j})\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$.    By Assertion~ef{cond:prop:time-set-A-7} of Proposition~ef{prop:time-set-A}, for $j=1,...,n-1$ there further exist $s_{j,1},...,s_{j,n_j}\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s_j}^{\mathrm{large}}=\mathring\mathcal{T}_{s_j}^{\mathrm{C},3}$ with $s_{j,1}=s_j$ and $s_{j,n_j}=s_{j+1}$, such that for $b=1,...,n_j-1$, $\{s_{j,b},s_{j,b+1}\}\in \mathring\mathcal{E}_\mathrm{T}$. Further using~\eqref{eq:cell-area} and Assertion~ef{cond:prop:time-set-A-2} of Proposition~ef{prop:time-set-A}, we have $s_j\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s_{j,b}}^\mathrm{large}$ and therefore $\partial\eta(\mathring I_{s_j})\subseteq \mathring H_{s_{j,b}}^\mathrm{large}$. Furthermore, since $\eta(\mathring I_{s_j})\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$, $\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_{s_j}))<\varepsilon r/3$ and $\ell$ has length at least $\varepsilon r$, we see that $\partial\eta(\mathring I_{s_j})\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$ and thus $\mathring H_{s_{j,b}}^\mathrm{large}\cap\ell
eq\emptyset$.    Therefore the collection of the cells $\mathring H_{s_{j,b}}^\mathrm{cell}$ form a path connecting $\mathring H_s^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring H_{s'}^\mathrm{cell}$ in $\mathring \mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$ and each   $\mathring H_{s_{j,b}}^\mathrm{large}$ intersects $\ell$. Furthermore, by another application of Assertion~ef{cond:prop:time-set-A-2} and  Assertion~ef{cond:prop:time-set-A-7} of Proposition~ef{prop:time-set-A}, $t\in  \mathring\mathcal{T}_s^\mathrm{cell}=\mathring\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}$, and there exists $t_1,...,t_m$ where $t_m=s$ and $t_1=t$ such that $\{t_j,t_{j+1}\}\in\mathring\mathcal{E}_\mathrm{T}$ for $j=1,...,m-1$ and $t_j \in \mathring\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},3}$. Therefore $\mathring H_{t_{j}}^\mathrm{cell}$ form a path connecting $\mathring H_s^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring H_{t}^\mathrm{cell}$ in $\mathring \mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$ and each   $\mathring H_{t_{j}}^\mathrm{large}$ intersects $\ell$. By the same argument, the same holds for $\mathring H_{s'}^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\mathring H_{t'}^\mathrm{cell}$.  This concludes the proof.

label: eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-000
title: Proof
body_md:
We only prove~\eqref{eq:thm-inv-circle} for $\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$; the proof for $\mathring \mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}$ is identical. Throughout the proof, $c>0$ is a constant that may vary line by line. We write $\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)$ for the a.s.\ unique time $t_0$ in $\mathring\mathcal{J}^-$   such that $0\in \mathring H_{t_0}^{\rm cell}$. Then following~\eqref{eq:cell-area},
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-000}\begin{split}
    \frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})^2}{\mathrm{area}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})}&\leq \frac{\big(\sum_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}} \mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))\big)^2}{\sum_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))/\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\leq \#\mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}\cdot \max_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}\cdot\frac{\sum_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}} \mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))^2}{\sum_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))}\\
    &\leq \#\mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}\cdot \max_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}\cdot \max_{s\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))}.
    \end{split}\end{equation}
    We further write $s_0$ for the a.s.\ unique time in $\mathring\mathcal{J}^-$ such that $0\in \mathring I_{s_0}$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J^-}, we have $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\mathring I_{s_0}\nsubseteq I(k/4) ]\lesssim 2^{-ck}$. By~\eqref{eq:cell-area}, we have $s_0\in\mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^\mathrm{cell}$, and by Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-2} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A}, $\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s_0}^{\mathrm{cell}}$. We write $\widetilde\mathcal{T}:=\cup_{t\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s_0}^{\mathrm{cell}}} \mathring\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}$, then
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-0}
         \frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})^2}{\mathrm{area}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})}\leq \big(\max_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}\big)^2\cdot \max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))}\bigg).
    \end{equation}
    Applying Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-5} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A} twice and a union bound, we have  
    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\widetilde\mathcal{T}\nsubseteq I(k/2)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}.$$
    Further combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J^-}, we have
     \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-1}\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\bigcup_{s\in\widetilde \mathcal{T}}\mathring I_s\nsubseteq I(k)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}.\end{equation}
    By~\eqref{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-1}, we may choose $c_1>0$ sufficiently large, such that for some $c'>0$,
    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\big[\bigcup_{s\in\widetilde \mathcal{T}}\mathring I_s\nsubseteq I(\lceil c_1\log M\rceil) \big]\leq c'M^{-p}.$$
    Combined with ~\eqref{lem:gap-J-min-B} and $\mathring\mathcal{J}^-\subseteq \mathcal{J}^-$, by a union bound, for some $c_2>0$,
    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\bigcup_{s\in\widetilde \mathcal{T}}\mathring I_s\subseteq I(\lceil c_1\log M \rceil),\ \min_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}}|\mathring I_s|\geq M^{-c_2}]\geq1- 2c'M^{-p}.$$
    Further by Lemma~\ref{lem:diam^2/area-E} and a union bound, we conclude that  for some constant $c'$,
    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\big[\max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))}\bigg)>M\big]\leq c'M^{-p}.$$
    This verifies that for each $p'\in(0,p)$, $$\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}\bigg[\max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta(\mathring I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta(\mathring I_s))}\bigg)^{p'}\bigg]<\infty.$$
    By~\eqref{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-1} along with Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-6} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A}, for large enough $k$, we have
    $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\max_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}>k^{28}]\lesssim 2^{-ck},$$
    which implies $\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}\big[\big(\max_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}\big)^p\big]<\infty$. Since $p>0$ is arbitrary, by~\eqref{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-000}, we infer that $\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}[\big( \frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})^2}{\mathrm{area}(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})}\big)^p]<\infty$ for every $p>0$. Further using $\deg(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})\leq \#\mathring\mathcal{T}_{\widehat\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{cell}}\leq \max_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}}\# \mathring\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ we have $\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}[\deg(\mathring H_0^{\rm cell})^p]<\infty$. This completes the proof.

label: lem:Euler
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Euler}
    Let $T$ be a disk triangulation without loops, and $\mathfrak{v}$ be a vertex on $T$. Let $f(\mathfrak{v})$ be the number of  faces of $T$ incident to $\mathfrak{v}$ (excluding the outer face), and $d(\mathfrak{v})$ be the number of vertices incident to $\mathfrak{v}$. Then $f(\mathfrak{v})\leq 2d(\mathfrak{v})-2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Consider the planar map $T_\mathfrak{v}$ formed by the  faces of $T$ that are incident to $\mathfrak{v}$ (excluding the outer face). By Euler's formula, $2\#\mathcal{E} T_\mathfrak{v} = 2\# \mathcal{F} T_\mathfrak{v}+2\# \mathcal{V} T_\mathfrak{v}-4$. There are exactly $f(\mathfrak{v})$ faces of $T$ incident to $\mathfrak{v}$ (excluding the outer face), and since $T$ has no loops, the remaining faces of $T_\mathfrak{v}$ has degree at least 2. Therefore $2\#\mathcal{E} T_\mathfrak{v}\geq 3f(\mathfrak{v}) + 2(\# \mathcal{F} T_\mathfrak{v}-f(\mathfrak{v}))$. This gives $f(\mathfrak{v})\leq 2\# \mathcal{V} T_\mathfrak{v}-4$, and the claim follows since $\# \mathcal{V} T_\mathfrak{v} = d(\mathfrak{v})+1$.

We only prove~\eqref{eq:thm-inv-circle-1} for $\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$; the proof for $ \mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large}$ is identical. By \cite[Lemma 5.29]{Tutte}, we have $\mathcal{T}_s^\mathrm{cell}\subseteq \widetilde\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{cell},\mathrm{inv}}\subseteq \widetilde\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}$ for each $s\in \mathcal{J}^-$. Then by~\eqref{eq:cell-area-0}, for each $t\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-prop:cell-moment-bound-000-A}\begin{split}
    \frac{\mathrm{diam}( H_t^{\rm cell})^2}{\mathrm{area}( H_t^{\rm cell})}&\leq \frac{2\big(\sum_{s\in \mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}} \mathrm{diam}(\eta( I_s))\big)^2}{\sum_{s\in \mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\mathrm{area}(\eta( I_s))/\# \mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell},\mathrm{inv}}}\leq 4\#\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}\cdot \max_{s\in \mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\#  \mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{cell},\mathrm{inv}}\cdot\frac{\sum_{s\in  \mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}} \mathrm{diam}(\eta( I_s))^2}{\sum_{s\in \mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{cell}}}\mathrm{area}(\eta( I_s))}\\
    &\leq 4\#\widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{C},1}\cdot \max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{C},1}}\# \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{C},1}\cdot \max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{C},1}}\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta( I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta( I_s))}\leq 4\big( \max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{C},1}}\# \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s}^{\mathrm{C},1}\big)^2 \cdot \max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t}^{\mathrm{C},1}}\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta( I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta( I_s))}
    \end{split}\end{equation}
    since $t\in\widetilde \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{C},1}_t$.
                                                                                       
 
 Recall the definition of $d_0^f$ and $\mathcal{H}_0^{\rm face}$ before Theorem~\ref{thm:invariance-uniformization}.   We write $\mathrm{cell}(0)$ for the a.s.\ unique time $t_0$ in $\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ such that $0\in H_{t_0}^\mathrm{cell}$. Now suppose $t\in \mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ such that $H_t^\mathrm{cell}\in \mathcal{H}_0^{\rm face}$. We write $s_{0,\mathrm{L}}\in\mathcal{J}_\mathrm{L}^-$ and $s_{0,\mathrm{R}}\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{R}$ for the a.s.\ unique time  such that $0\in I_{s_{0,\mathrm{L}}}\cap I_{s_{0,\mathrm{R}}}$. Then we have $\{s_{0,\mathrm{L}},s_{0,\mathrm{R}}\}\cap \mathcal{T}_{ \mathrm{cell}(0)}^\mathrm{cell}\neq\emptyset$. Following Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-0-3} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A-0}, we have $s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1}$ if and only if $t\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}$, which further implies that $\mathrm{cell}(0)\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s_{0,\mathrm{L}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}\cup \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s_{0,\mathrm{R}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Now by Proposition~\ref{prop:Tutte5.8}, Proposition~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J^-} holds for $\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ or $\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{R}$ in place of $\mathring\mathcal{J}^-$, and therefore we have $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\{s_{0,\mathrm{L}},s_{0,\mathrm{R}}\}\nsubseteq I(k)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}$. Let
 $$\widetilde\mathcal{T}_1 =\bigcup_{t_0\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s_{0,\mathrm{L}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}\cup \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{s_{0,\mathrm{R}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}}  \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{t_0}^{\mathrm{C},1} \ \ \text{, } \ \ \  \widetilde\mathcal{T}_2 =\bigcup_{t\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_1} \mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1} \ \ \text{ ,  } \ \ \ \widetilde\mathcal{T}_3 = \bigcup_{u\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_2} \mathcal{T}_u^{\mathrm{C},1}  \ \ \text{ and  } \ \ \  \widetilde\mathcal{T}_4 = \bigcup_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_3} \mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1} .  $$
 It follows that for each pair $(s,t)$ such that $s\in \widetilde \mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $t\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{cell}(0)}^{\mathrm{C},1}$, $s\in\widetilde \mathcal{T}_3$.
 By iteratively applying Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-0-5} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A-0}, we have $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\widetilde\mathcal{T}_3\nsubseteq I(6k)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}$ and $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\widetilde\mathcal{T}_4\nsubseteq I(8k)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}$, and furthermore
 $$\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\bigg[  \bigcup_{s\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}_3} I_s\nsubseteq I(7k)   \bigg]\lesssim 2^{-ck} $$
 for some $c>0$. Following the same proof as Proposition~\ref{prop:moment-bound-1}, using Lemma~\ref{lem:diam^2/area-E} and Lemma~\ref{lem:gap-J-min}, we conclude that for every $p'\in (0,p)$,
  $$\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}\bigg[\max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_3}\bigg(\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\eta(  I_s))^2}{\mathrm{area}(\eta( I_s))}\bigg)^{p'}\bigg]<\infty.$$
  Using $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}[\widetilde\mathcal{T}_4\nsubseteq I(8k)]\lesssim 2^{-ck}$ and Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-0-6} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A-0}, we conclude that 
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:degreeeeeee-new}\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\big[\max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_3} \#\widetilde\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}\geq k^{60}\big]\lesssim 2^{-ck},\end{equation}
  and therefore $\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}\big[ \big(\max_{s\in \widetilde\mathcal{T}_3} \#\widetilde\mathcal{T}_s^{\mathrm{C},1}\big)^p \big]<\infty$. 

  Now consider a time $t\in\mathcal{J}^-$ and let $\mathfrak{v}_t$ be its vertex in $T$ with degree $d$. Since there are exactly $d$ triangular faces incident to $\mathfrak{v}_t$ and $T$ has no loops, by Lemma~\ref{lem:Euler} and Assertion~\ref{cond:prop:time-set-A-0-3} of Proposition~\ref{prop:time-set-A-0}, $d\leq 2\#\mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  Therefore for each cell $H_t\in \mathcal{H}$, since its degree in the primal map $M$ is bounded by its degree in the triangulation $T$, we have $\deg(H_t)\leq 2\#\mathcal{T}_t^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and~\eqref{eq:degreeeeeee-new} implies that $\mathbb{E}\big[\max_{H\in\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{face}}_0}(\deg(H))^p\big]<\infty$.
  Since $p>0$ is arbitrary, we have verified that 
  $$\mathbb{E}\Big[ \max_{H\in \mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{face}}_0}\Big(\frac{\mathrm{diam}(H)^2}{\mathrm{area}(H)}\big(\deg(H)\big)^q\Big)\Big]<\infty $$
  for any $q>0$. Finally, for any $t^f\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{R}$ such that $\{t^f,\mathrm{cell}(0)\}\in\mathcal{E}_\mathrm{T}$, we have $t^f\in\widetilde\mathcal{T}_3$ and $\deg(t^f)\leq 2\# \mathcal{T}_{t^f}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Then by an identical argument as above, $\mathbb{E}_\mathrm{E}[(d_0^f)^q]<\infty$ for any $q>0$. This finishes the proof.

The  claim (i) is immediate from construction of the space-filling SLE curve in~\cite[Section 4.2]{ig4}.
 
 For the claim (ii), first assume $\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u<L_s$ choose the largest integer $k'<k$ such that $\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k',\mathrm{L}}]}L_u>\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$                                                        
 where recall that $s_{0,\mathrm{L}}=s$. Then $\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k'+1,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u=\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$,   $\inf_{u\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u< \inf_{u\in[s,s_{k',\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$ and $\inf_{u\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u = \inf_{u\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k'+1,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$.
 For $t\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k'+1,\mathrm{L}}]$, $\mathcal{L}_t\geq \mathcal{L}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}-1$, and therefore $$L_{t}\geq  L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}-\sup_{u\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},t]}|(L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}} - \mathcal{L}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}) - (L_u-\mathcal{L}_u)|-1> L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}} -\Delta_\mathrm{L}[s_{k',\mathrm{L}},t],$$
 which implies that $s_{k'+1,\mathrm{L}}< \tau_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and hence  $s_{k,\mathrm{L}}< \tau_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. In particular, $L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}} -  \Delta_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}< \inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u \leq L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}$. Suppose $t> s_{k',\mathrm{L}}$, $t\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ and $w\in I_t$ such that $\eta(w)$ is in the interior of segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])$ between $z_{k',\mathrm{L}}$ and $z_{k,\mathrm{L}}$. Then $\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u\leq L_w\leq L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}$, $w<s_{k,\mathrm{L}}$, which implies that $t\leq \tau_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and thus $t\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. On the other hand, since $\mathcal{L}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}<\mathcal{L}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}$, 
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-close-0900} L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}\leq  L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}+\sup_{u\in [s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}|(L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}} - \mathcal{L}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}) - (L_u-\mathcal{L}_u)| \leq  L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}+ \Delta_\mathrm{L}[s_{k',\mathrm{L}},s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]\leq L_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}}}+\Delta_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1} \end{equation}
 where we used $s_{k'+1,\mathrm{L}}< \tau_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ in the last step. Thus $s_{k,\mathrm{L}}\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k',\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and we further have $t\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}\subseteq \mathcal{T}_{\widetilde s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}^\mathrm{cell}$ and $\partial\eta(I_t)\subseteq H_{\widetilde s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}^\mathrm{cell}$.  This proves claim (ii). If $\inf_{u\in[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u=L_s$, then clearly $s_{k,\mathrm{L}}<\tau_{s,\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}\geq L_s$.    Replacing $s_{k',\mathrm{L}}$ in~\eqref{eq:pf-close-0900} with $s$ then gives $s_{k,\mathrm{L}}\in \mathcal{T}_{s,\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$.  Let $s'' = \inf\{u\geq s:u\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}\}$. Then $s''\in \mathcal{T}_{s,\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$  and therefore $s''\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $\partial\eta(I_{s''})\subseteq H_{\widetilde s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}^\mathrm{cell}$. Then claim (ii) for this case also follows since $z_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}} = z_{s_{k-1,\mathrm{L}}} = \eta(s)$ and $s\in I_{s''}$.

                                                                  
 For the claim (iii), by claim~(\ref{cond:thm:KMT-0-cone-(ii)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:KMT-0-cone}, \cite[Lemma 5.9, Lemma 5.10]{Tutte} and the Borel-Contelli lemma, there is some constant $C>1$ such that for every large enough $n$, $\sup_{u\in [-2^{2n},2^{2n}]}|L_u-\mathcal{L}_u|\leq Cn$. We work in this setting. By our definition, we have $$\ell_{s,k,\mathrm{L}} = L_s - \inf_{u\in [s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]} L_u, \ \ \inf_{u\in [s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]} \mathcal{L}_u  = \mathcal{L}_s-k.$$
 Then $$|\ell_{s,k,\mathrm{L}}-k|\leq \sup_{u\in [s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}|(L_s-\mathcal{L}_s) - (L_u-\mathcal{L}_u)|\leq 2Cn$$
 since $[s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]\subseteq [-2^n,2^n]$. This finishes the proof of the first part.

body_md:
Below we assume $r$ is sufficiently large.    By Proposition~\ref{prop:property-CH}, the conditions in Theorem~\ref{thm:CellSystemPack} holds for  $(\mathring\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell},\mathring \mathcal{H}^\mathrm{large})$, and claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}) follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:CellSystemPack}. Note that for $t\in\mathcal{J}^-$, $\mathfrak{tr}(t)$ is in the convex hull of the union of the disk for $\mathfrak{v}_t$ and its neighboring disks, so~\eqref{eq:E-pack} is a consequence of claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}), ~\eqref{eq:E-curve-pack} and a triangle inequality. Now we prove~\eqref{eq:E-curve-pack}. Let $t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $\eta(t)\in B(0;r)$. Let $t_0 = \sup\{u\leq t:u\in\mathring\mathcal{J}\}$,   $t_\mathrm{L}^+$ be the left  endpoint of $\mathfrak{e}_{t_0}$, and $ t^+ = \inf\{u> t_0: u\in\mathring\mathcal{J}^-\}$. Following Lemma~\ref{lem:time-set-sew}, we have $t_\mathrm{L}^+\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{t_0,\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and by~\eqref{eq:def-TtCd-mr-0}, $t^+\in  \mathring\mathcal{T}_{t_0,\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$, and therefore by~\eqref{eq:def-TtCd-mr} we have $t^+\in \mathring\mathcal{T}_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Since $t\in\mathring I_{t^+}$, by Corollary~\ref{cor:eta-boundary}, $\partial \eta(\mathring I_{t^+})\cap B(0;r)\neq\emptyset$. By~\eqref{eq:cell-area}, we have $\partial\eta(\mathring I_{t^+})\subseteq \mathring H_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}^\mathrm{cell}$ and in particular  $\mathring H_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}^\mathrm{cell}\cap B(0;r)\neq\emptyset$. Furthermore, by Lemma~\ref{lem:GMS2.9}, for large enough $r$, we have $\mathrm{diam}(\mathring H_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}^\mathrm{cell})<0.1\varepsilon r$ and thus $|\eta(t)-c(\mathring H_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}^\mathrm{cell})|\leq 0.1\varepsilon r$. Therefore by Theorem~\ref{thm:CellSystemPack},  {up to a reflection of $\mathcal{P}$, for each $t$ such that $\eta(t)\in B(0;r)$,} $|\eta(t)-o(\mathfrak{v}_{t_\mathrm{L}^+})|<0.2\varepsilon r$ for $r$ large enough. By a translation, we may further assume that the disk for the cell $\mathring H_0^\mathrm{cell}$ is centered at 0, which does not affect the pervious convergence. On the other hand, $\mathfrak{tr}(t)$ is in the convex hull of the union of the disk for $\mathfrak{v}_{t_\mathrm{L}^+}$ and its neighboring disks. This along with claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}) applied to $B(0;3r)$ and a triangle inequality gives~\eqref{eq:E-curve-pack}, which completes the proof for (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(ii)})  {up to a possible reflection of $\mathcal{P}$}.
    
    


    To prove claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}), let $s,t\in\mathring\mathcal{J}$ such that $\eta([s,t])\subseteq B(0;r)$.   By~\eqref{eq:E-curve-pack} and claim  (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}), all the disks for the vertices of $T_{s,t}$ are contained within $B(0;1.5 r)$ if we assume $r$ is large enough. Let $\mathfrak{v}=\mathfrak{v}_{x_{j,q}}$ be a boundary vertex of $T_{s,t}$ that is on an edge $\mathfrak{e}_u$ where $u\in [s,t]$. Let $\widetilde s\in\mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ such that $\mathfrak{v}_{\widetilde s}$ is also on the edge $\mathfrak{e}_u$. Following the identical argument as in the previous paragraph, using Lemma~\ref{lem:time-set-sew}, ~\eqref{eq:def-TtCd}, for  $u' = \inf\{u_1\geq u: u_1\in\mathcal{J}^-\}$, we have $u',\widetilde s\in \mathcal{T}_u^{\mathrm{C},1,0}$ and therefore $u'\in \mathcal{T}_{\widetilde s}^{\mathrm{C},1}$.  Then by~\eqref{eq:cell-area-0},  $\partial\eta(I_{u'})\subseteq H_{\widetilde s}^\mathrm{cell}$, and by Corollary~\ref{cor:eta-boundary}, $H_{\widetilde s}^\mathrm{cell}\cap B(0;r)\neq\emptyset$.
    By Lemma~\ref{lem:GMS2.9} applied to $\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$, for $r$ large enough $\mathrm{diam} (H_{\widetilde s}^\mathrm{cell})<0.1\varepsilon r$. By claim~(\ref{cond:lem:construction-embed-cell-0-(ii)}) of Lemma~\ref{lem:construction-embed-cell-0}, the  corresponding segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,x])$ between $z_{x_{j,q}}$ and $z_{x_{j-1,q}}$ is contained within the convex hull of $H_{\widetilde s}^\mathrm{cell}$ and has diameter less than $0.1\varepsilon r$. Then $|\eta(u) - z_{x_{j,q}}|\leq \mathrm{diam}(H_{\widetilde s}^\mathrm{cell})<0.1\varepsilon r$. By~\eqref{eq:E-curve-pack}, $|\eta(u)-\mathfrak{tr}(u)|\leq 0.1\varepsilon r$ for $r$ large enough, while by claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}) applied to $B(0;3r)$, since $\mathfrak{tr}(u)$ is within the convex hull of the union of the disk for $\mathfrak{v}$ and its neighboring disks,   $|\mathfrak{tr}(u)-o(\mathfrak{v})|\leq 0.1\varepsilon r$. Thus $|z_{x_{j,q}}-o(\mathfrak{v})|\leq 0.4\varepsilon r$. This verifies the first part of claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}) up to a global reflection of $\mathcal{P}$.

    
                                                                                                                                                                                 
 To prove the last sentence of claim  (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}), again by claim~(\ref{cond:lem:construction-embed-cell-0-(ii)}) of Lemma~\ref{lem:construction-embed-cell-0}, the segment of the left boundary of $\eta((-\infty,s])$ from $\eta(s)$ to $z_{s_{1,\mathrm{L}}}$ is contained in the convex hull of $H_{{s_{1,\mathrm{L}}}}^\mathrm{cell}$ and therefore has diameter less than $\varepsilon r$ for all large enough $r$, which implies claim  (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}) for $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ if $i_1=1$, since in this case $t<s_{1,\mathrm{L}}$. If $i_1\geq2$, $s_{i_1-1,\mathrm{L}}\in [s,t]$. Then $z_{s_{i_1-1,\mathrm{L}}}$, the leftmost point of $\eta([s,t])$ and $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$  are on the left boundary of $\eta((-\infty,s]))$ and ordered from right to left, while by the same argument, using claim (\ref{cond:lem:construction-embed-cell-0-(ii)}) of Lemma~\ref{lem:construction-embed-cell-0},  this segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s]))$ between $z_{s_{i_1-1,\mathrm{L}}}$ and $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ is contained within the convex hull of some cell $H^\mathrm{cell}\in\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{cell}$ that intersects $B(0;r)$ and therefore has diameter less than $\varepsilon r$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:GMS2.9}. This gives the desired closeness between $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ and the leftmost point of $\eta([s,t])$. Now we prove the analogous result for $z_{t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}}$. Assume $\inf_{u\in [s,s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]} L_u< L_s$ and let $k$ be the largest integer such that $\inf_{u\in [s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]} L_u> \inf_{u\in [s,s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$.    Then the same argument as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:construction-embed-cell-0} implies that $L_u\geq L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}} - \Delta_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ for $u\in [s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]$, $s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}<\tau_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ and $s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Furthermore, $t\in [s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]$ and $\inf_{u\in [s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]} L_u<\inf_{u\in [s,s_{k,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$ and therefore $-\Delta_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}<\inf_{u\in [s,t]}L_u-L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}\leq 0$. On the other hand, by the sewing procedure, $\mathcal{L}_{t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}}\leq \mathcal{L}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}$ and $t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}\in [s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]$, and similar to~\eqref{eq:pf-close-0900}, we have $L_{t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}}\leq L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}+\Delta_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Observe that $\eta([s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}])$ covers  the segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,t])$ between $z_{s,t,\mathrm{L}}^-$ and $z_{t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}}$. Suppose $u\in \mathcal{J}^-_\mathrm{L}$ such that for some $w\in I_u\cap[s_{k,\mathrm{L}},s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]$,   $\eta(w)$ is on this segment.  Then  $L_w$ is between $\inf_{u\in [s,t]}L_u$ and $\inf_{u\in [t,t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}]}L_u$, where both are values are in $[L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}-\Delta_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1},L_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}}}+\Delta_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}]$. Furthermore, $u\leq s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}} \leq \tau_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. Thus $u\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$, which combined with $s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{k,\mathrm{L}},\mathrm{L}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$ gives $u\in \mathcal{T}_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}^{\mathrm{C},1}$. By~\eqref{eq:cell-area-0}, $\partial\eta(I_u)\subseteq H_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}^\mathrm{cell}$, and since $u$ is arbitrary, this further implies that the segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,t])$ between $z_{s,t,\mathrm{L}}^-$ and $z_{t_{j_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ is within the convex hull of  $H_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}^\mathrm{cell}$ and hence has diameter less than $\varepsilon r$ if we assume $r$ is large enough. The case where  $\inf_{u\in [s,s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}]} L_u= L_s$ can be handled analogously, where the same proof above works with $s$ in place of $s_{k,\mathrm{L}}$.
 
 
 The same applies for $z_{s_{i_2,\mathrm{R}}}$, $z_{t_{j_2,\mathrm{R}}}$ and the rightmost point of $\eta([s,t])$. This verifies the claim  (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}) {up to a possible reflection of $\mathcal{P}$}. {Now suppose with $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}$-probability, the claim (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(ii)}) and (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)})   hold for the reflection of $\mathcal{P}$. Assume $p>0$. By the scale invariance in Lemma~\ref{lem:Rb},  we may choose some constant $c>0$ small enough, then with  $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}$-probability $1-p/2$, for some large $r>0$, $B(0;cr)\subseteq \eta([s_n,t_n])\subseteq B(0;c^{-1}r)$ where $s_n = \inf(\mathring\mathcal{J}\cap [-2^n,\infty))$ and  $t_n = \inf(\mathring\mathcal{J}\cap [2^n,\infty))$. We fix $r$ large enough and work with the intersection between two events, which has positive probability. Let $\gamma_{s_n,t_n}$ be an $o(r)$-perturbation of the curve formed by the points $z_{x_{i,q}}$ and segments of $\partial((-\infty,s_n]))\cup\partial((-\infty,t_n]))$, such that it is a simple curve and forms an  embedding of $\partial T_{s_n,t_n}$ with the same orientation as on the planar map $T$. Let $\gamma_{s_n,t_n}'$ be the embedded curve for $\partial T_{s_n,t_n}$  formed by joining the centers of adjacent disks in $\mathcal{P}$ for vertices on $\partial T_{s_n,t_n}$ with line segments, which also preserves the orientation.   The curves  $\gamma_{s_n,t_n}$ and  $\widetilde\gamma'_{s_n,t_n}$ have distance at most $4\varepsilon r$ when viewed as curve modulo time parameterizations, where $\widetilde\gamma'_{s_n,t_n}$ is   the reflection of $\gamma'_{s_n,t_n}$ , and using $B(0;cr)\subseteq \eta([s_n,t_n])$, the two curves must have the same winding number around 0.  Since we have centered the disk for $\mathring H_0^\mathrm{cell}$ at 0 in $\mathcal{P}$, $\gamma_{s_n,t_n}$ and  $\gamma'_{s_n,t_n}$ must have the same winding number around 0. This is a contradiction and thus $p=0$. This finishes the proof for claims (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)})-(\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}).
}

    To prove the claim  (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iv)}), by~\eqref{eq:SLE-contain-ball-1}, ~\eqref{eq:SLE-contained-in-ball-1} and the Borel-Contelli lemma, a.s.\ for each $\delta>0$, for large enough $n$, $B(0;2^{(\frac{1}{\gamma Q}-\delta)n})\subseteq \eta([-2^n,2^n])\subseteq B(0;2^{(\frac{1}{\gamma Q}+\delta)n})$. One can further infer that for some $\beta>0$, a.s.\ for large enough $r>0$, $B(0;4r)\subseteq \eta([-r^\beta,r^\beta])\subseteq B(0;r^{1+\delta})$ and therefore if $\eta([s,t])\subseteq B(0;r)$ then $s,t\in [-2^m,2^m]$ where $m\leq 10\beta\log r$. Since $s_{i_1-1,\mathrm{L}}\leq t$ and $t_{j,\mathrm{L}}\leq s_{i_1+1,\mathrm{L}}$ for $j=1,...,j_1$,  {by \cite[Lemma 5.10]{Tutte}, part~(\ref{cond:thm:KMT-0-cone-(ii)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:KMT-0-cone} and Borel-Contelli lemma, for some constant $C_1>0$,} almost surely for large enough $m$, $\sup_{u\in [-2^{2m},2^{2m}]}|L_u-\mathcal{L}_u|\leq Cm $, and for every $u\in\mathcal{J}\cap[-2^m,2^m]$, $\inf\{u'\geq u: \mathcal{L}_{u'}<\mathcal{L}_u-3\}<2^{2m}$,  $\inf\{u'\geq u: \mathcal{R}_{u'}<\mathcal{R}_u-3\}<2^{2m}$. Then for $r$ large enough, all the times $s,t$ and $x_{j,q}$ are within $[-2^{2m},2^{2m}]$ with $m\leq 10\beta\log r$. We work with this setting.

For the last claim, suppose $q=\mathrm{L}$ and $z_{x_{k,\mathrm{L}}}$ is on $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])\backslash\partial\eta([s,t])$. Then the segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])$ between $z_{x_{k,\mathrm{L}}}$ and $z_{s,t,\mathrm{L}}^-$ is contained with in the segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])$ between $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ and $z_{s,t,\mathrm{L}}^-$ so we may assume $x=s,k=i_1$. Now the quantum length of the segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])$ between $\eta(s)$ and $z_{s,t,\mathrm{L}}^-$ is equal to $L_s-\inf_{u\in[s,t]}L_u$, whereas $i_1 = 1+\mathcal{L}_s-\inf_{u\in [s,t]}\mathcal{L}_u$. Then 
    $$|L_s-\inf_{u\in[s,t]}L_u - (1+\mathcal{L}_s-\inf_{u\in [s,t]}\mathcal{L}_u)|\leq 1+\sup_{u\in[s,t]}|L_s-L_u-(\mathcal{L}_s-\mathcal{L}_u)|\leq 1+6Cm.$$
    The last claim then follows from the first part of (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iv)}) as the quantum length of the  segment of $\partial\eta((-\infty,s])$ between $\eta(s)$ and $z_{s_{i_1,\mathrm{L}}}$ is in $[i_1-C\log r,i_1+C\log r]$.

body_md:
\label{def:unif-convergence}
    Let  $D,D^n\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ be Jordan domains such that the Hausdorff distance between $\overline {D^n}$ and $\overline D$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$.   Let $f^n:\overline {D^n} {\to\mathbb{C}}$ and $f:\overline D\to\mathbb{C}$.   We say $f^n$ converges to $f$ uniformly, if for each $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\delta>0$ and $N>0$, such that for each $n>N$, $z'\in \overline {D^n}$ and $z\in \overline D$ with $|z'-z|<\delta$, we have $|f^n(z')-f(z)|<\varepsilon$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The first claim is immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:def-cZ^n} and Theorem~\ref{thm:KMT-0-cone}. For the second claim, let  $\Phi_\mathrm{T}(\mathcal{Z}^n) = ( T^n,{\mathfrak{tr}^n})$, and let $\eta^n$ be the space-filling curve generated via the boundary length process  $(2^{n/2}Z_{2^{-n}t})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$.    Let $\mathcal{J}^{n,-}$ and $\mathring\mathcal{J}^{n,-}$ be the downward jump times defined in the same way as $\mathcal{J}^-$ and $\mathring\mathcal{J}^-$ for $\mathcal{Z}^n$, and $t\mapsto \mathfrak{v}_t^n$ be the bijection between $\mathcal{J}^{n,-}$ and $\mathcal{V} T^n$.  Note that from the scaling in Lemma~\ref{lem:Rb}, $\eta^n(t) = \mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}^{-1}\eta(2^{-n}t)$, and the downward jump times for $(\mathcal{Z}^n_{2^{-n}t})_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ is equal to $2^n\mathcal{J}^{n,-}$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:def-cZ^n} and Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell} applied to $r = \mathrm{diam}(\eta^n([-2^{n+1},2^{n+1}])) = \mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}^{-1}\mathrm{diam}(\eta([-2,2]))$, as we scale by  $\mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}$, there is a circle packing for $  T^n$ such that   in probability as $n\to\infty$,
    \begin{align}
 &  \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{ \mathrm{diam}(\eta([-2,2])) }\sup\{ |\eta(t)-o(\mathfrak{v}_t^n)|: t\in \mathcal{J}^{n,-},t\in [-2,2]\} = 0;  \label{eq:E-pack-0-0}  \\ & 
   \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{ \mathrm{diam}(\eta([-2,2]))}\sup\{ |\eta(t)-{\mathfrak{tr}^n}(t)|: t\in [-2,2]\} = 0,  \label{eq:E-pack-0-1}
\end{align}
where the limit~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-1} is uniform over all choices of the space-filling curve $\mathfrak{tr}^n$. This along with part (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(i)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell} implies that the maximal diameter of disks for vertices incident to the faces for times in $[-2,2]$ tends to 0 in probability. Fix a compact set $K$ as in the statement and $(a,b,a',b')\in K$.  Also choose any deterministic sequence $(a'_n,b'_n,a_n,b_n)\in K$ such that $(a'_n,b'_n,a_n,b_n)\to (a',b',a,b)$.  Let $I = I_{a',b'}(0)$ and the interval $I_{a,b}$ for $I$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT} with its middlepoint $t_{\rm mid}$. Define $I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)$ and $I_{a_n,b_n}$ analogously. Let $I_n'$ be the interval $I'$ defined for $I = I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)$ in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT}. By Proposition~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J^-} and the scaling from Lemma~\ref{lem:def-cZ^n},  with probability tending to 1 as $n\to\infty$,   $\mathring\mathcal{J}^{n,-}$ intersects both components of $I_{a_n',b_n'}\backslash I_{a_n,b_n}$, and the length of the interval $|I_n'|\to |I_{a,b}|$   in probability.  By    Lemma~\ref{lem:A2},  $ \Phi_{\rm simple}(\mathcal{Z}^n)|_{I_{a_n,b_n}} =   \Phi_{\rm simple}(\mathcal{Z}^n|_{I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)})|_{I_{a_n,b_n}}$, and therefore  the simple version  $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T_{n,I'_n})$ as in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT} can be viewed as a submap of $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T^n)$. 

Let $t_{\rm mid}' =  \inf\{u\geq t_{\rm mid}:u\in \mathring\mathcal{J}^{n,-}\}$. Then as $n\to\infty$, $t_{\rm mid}'\in \mathring\mathcal{J}^{n,-} $ with probability tending to 1, and $t_{\rm mid}'\to t_{\rm mid}$ in probability by  Lemma~\ref{lem:A2} and Proposition~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J^-}. The convergence in~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-1} and $t_{\rm mid}'\to t_{\rm mid}$ implies that with probability tending to 1, $\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'}$ is an interior vertex of $T_{n,I_n'}$.    Let $D=\eta(I_{a,b})$, $\widetilde D=\mathbb{D}$, $\mathcal{P}^n$ is the circle packing for $T^n$ restricted to vertices in  $T_{n,I_n'}$  and thus a circle embedding for $T_{n,I_n'}$, and $\widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$ is a   circle packing in $\mathbb{D}$ for $ T_{n,I_n'}$ centered at the vertex $\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'}$.   Let $f^{n,0}$ be a homeomorphism between the carriers of $\mathcal{P}^n$ and $\widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$ that corresponds disks and send centers of disks to the  corresponding centers.                                                                                                               
  Note that $\eta(I_{a,b})$ is a Jordan domain by the construction of the space-filling curve $\eta$ via GFF flow line as in~\cite{ig4}. Below we apply Theorem~\ref{thm:He-Schramm-extension-1} for $\mathcal{P}^n$ and $\widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$.

Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(i)}) is true since the maximal diameter of disks for vertices $\mathfrak{v}_t^n$ where $t\in [-2,2]\cap  \mathcal{J}^{n,-}$ and the disks tangent to them tends to 0 in probability. By part (\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iii)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell}, the curve distance~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0} between $\partial \mathrm{carrier}(\mathcal{P}^n)$ and $\partial\eta(I_n')$ tends to 0 in probability. Using $|I_n'|\to |I_{a,b}|$ in probability and the continuity of the curve $\eta$,   the two components of $\eta(I_{a,b}\backslash I_n')\cup\eta(I_n'\backslash I_{a,b})$ are contained within a small neighborhood of the two endpoints of $\eta(I_{a,b})$ and thus the curve distance~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0} between $\partial\eta(I_n')$ and  $\partial\eta(I_{a,b})$  tends to 0. Thus   the curve distance~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0} between $\partial \mathrm{carrier}(\mathcal{P}^n)$ and $\partial\eta(I_{a,b})$ tends to 0 in probability as $n\to\infty$ as well. This along with Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(i)}) implies both Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(ii)}) and Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(iv)}) for $\mathcal{P}^n$.  Moreover, by continuity of $\eta$ and~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-0}, $|\eta(t_{\rm mid}) - o(\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'})|\leq |\eta(t_{\rm mid})-\eta(t'_{\rm mid})|+|\eta(t'_{\rm mid})-o(\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'})|\to 0$.  Then Conditions~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(i)}), (\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(ii)}) and  (\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(iv)}) remain true if we translate $\mathcal{P}^n$ such that the disk for $\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'}$ is now centered at $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$. We write $g^n(z) = f^{n,0}(z - \eta(t_{\rm mid})+o(\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'})) $.    Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(iii)}) then holds for $p_0=\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ after the translation of $\mathcal{P}^n$ since $g^n(p_0)=0$ by our choice of embedding of $\widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$.  Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(ii)}) for $\widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$ is immediate since the circle packing is in $\mathbb{D}$.

Now by Theorem~\ref{thm:He-Schramm-extension-1}, since Conditions~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(i)})-(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(iii)}) hold, the maximal diameter of disks in $\mathcal{P}_{n,I_n'} =  \widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$ tends to 0 in probability, which further implies  Condition~(\ref{cond:thm:He-Schramm-extension-1-(iv)}) for $ \widetilde\mathcal{P}^n$ since the packing is in $\partial \mathbb{D}$. Further by Theorem~\ref{thm:He-Schramm-extension-1}, up to a rotation, the maps $g^n$ converges uniformly to a conformal map $\varphi_{I_{a,b}}:\eta(I_{a,b})\to\mathbb{D}$ sending $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ to 0, while by Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-perturb}, up to a rotation, the conformal map $\varphi_{I_n'}:\eta(I_n')\to\mathbb{D}$ sending $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ to 0 converges uniformly to $\varphi_{I_{a,b}}$ in probability. The uniformity of the limit~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-1} over the trace $\mathfrak{tr}$ and the choice that $\eta_{n,I_n'}$ starts from 1 further imply that the tangent point between $\partial\mathbb{D}$ and the disk in $\mathcal{P}_{n,I_n'}$ for the left endpoint of the root edge of $T_{n,I_n'}$ is in $o_n(1)$ distance from 1 in probability.  This along with ~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-0} and ~\eqref{eq:E-pack-0-1} verifies  Conditions~\ref{cond:def:CPtoMOT-0}-\ref{cond:def:CPtoMOT-2} in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT} for $\mathcal{P}_{n,I_n'}$ and $(I_{a_n,b_n},I_n')$, since recentering the packing $\mathcal{P}_{n,I_n'}$ at the corresponding midpoint vertex for $I_{a_n,b_n}$ instead of $\mathfrak{v}_{t_{\rm mid}'}$ and rotating $\mathcal{P}_{n,I_n'}$ such that the disk for the vertex to the left of the root edge is tangent to $\partial\mathbb{D}$ at 1 only change the error by $o_n(1)$. For  Condition~\ref{cond:def:CPtoMOT-3}, note that by ~\eqref{eq:Rb-bound}, $2^{-n/2}\log(\mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}^{-1}\mathrm{diam}(\eta([-2,2])))\to 0$ in probability as $n\to\infty$. Let $I_n' = [s_n,t_n]$, and $z_{s_n,t_n,q}^-$, $z_{x_{k,q}}^n$ where $q\in\{\mathrm{L},\mathrm{R}\}$, $x\in\{s,t\}$ be the points defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell} for $[s,t]=[s_n,t_n]$. We further move the points  $z_{x_{k,q}}^n$ that are not on $\partial\eta(I_n')$ to $z_{s_n,t_n,q}^-$. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
Conditions~\ref{cond:def:CPtoMOT-3} in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT} then follows by  the uniform convergence of map $g^n$ and the conformal map $\varphi_{I_n'}$ to the conformal map $\varphi_{I_{a,b}}$ and the bound in part~(\ref{cond:thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell-(iv)}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-pack-Hcell}. This gives that for any $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\big[\mathrm{err}(\mathcal{Z}^n|_{I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)},Z^n|_{I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)},a_n,b_n)>\varepsilon\big]\to 0$, which implies the desired convergence of circle packing to mating of trees by setting $(a_n',b_n',a_n,b_n)=(a',b',a,b)$ and also~\eqref{eq:410uniform}, since otherwise by compactness there will be deterministic $(a_n',b_n',a_n,b_n)$ and $\varepsilon_0,\delta_0>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}_\mathrm{E}\big[\mathrm{err}(\mathcal{Z}^n|_{I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)},Z^n|_{I_{a_n',b_n'}(0)}, a_n,b_n)>\varepsilon_0\big]\to \delta_0$, which is a contradiction.

    where $\xi_{an}$ is a Poisson$(an)$ random variable. Let $\delta\in(0,0.1)$ be small. Fix $\delta'\in(0,1)$. We pick deterministic constants $0<\varepsilon_3 <\varepsilon_1<\varepsilon<\delta$ sufficiently small (depending on $\delta$), such that as $\delta\to0$, with probability tending to 1, we have
    \begin{align*}
       &                                                                   
       \inf_{s\in [A\varepsilon_1,A\varepsilon]} L_s < \inf_{s\in [0,A\varepsilon_1]}L_s-\varepsilon_3; \ \ \inf_{s\in [A\varepsilon,A\delta]} L_s< \inf_{s\in [0,A\varepsilon]}L_s-\varepsilon_3; \ \ \inf_{s\in [0,A\delta]} L_s> 1-\delta'; \\ &                                                                     
       \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon_1)]} L_s < \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon)]}L_s-\varepsilon_3; \ \ \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon)]} L_s < \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\delta)]}L_s-\varepsilon_3; \ \ \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\delta)]} L_s< \delta'.
    \end{align*}
    Then using part~(\ref{cond:lem:disk-pf-0-(v)}) from Lemma~\ref{lem:disk-pf-0}, with probability tending to 1 as $n\to\infty$ sufficiently faster than $\delta\to0$, 
    \begin{align}
       &                                                                           
       \inf_{s\in [A\varepsilon_1,A\varepsilon]} \widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n < \inf_{s\in [0,A\varepsilon_1]}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n; \ \ \inf_{s\in [A\varepsilon,A\delta]} \widetilde\mathcal{L}^n_s< \inf_{s\in [0,A\varepsilon]}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n-\varepsilon_3\sqrt n/2; \ \ \inf_{s\in [0,A\delta]} \widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n> (1-2\delta')n^{1/2}; \label{eq:lem:disk-pf-1-1} \\ &                                                                              
       \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon_1)]} \widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n < \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon)]}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n-\varepsilon_3\sqrt n/2; \ \ \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\varepsilon)]} \widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n < \inf_{s\in [0,A(1-\delta)]}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_s^n<2\delta' n^{1/2}.\label{eq:lem:disk-pf-1-2} 
    \end{align}
 We work in this setting.   Let $\mathring B^n$ be the  $B^n$ minus all the intervals $(t^-,t^+]$ such that~\eqref{eq:double-edge-Mullin} holds for $(\widetilde\mathcal{L}^n,\widetilde\mathcal{R}^n)$ in place of $(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{R})$.

Let $t_\varepsilon^- = \inf\{s\geq A\varepsilon:s\in\mathring B^n\}$, $t_\varepsilon^+ = \sup\{s\leq A(1-\varepsilon): s\in\mathring B^n\}$ and $I'=[t_\varepsilon^-,t_\varepsilon^+]$. Then $[A\delta,A(1-\delta)]\subseteq I'$. Let $T_{n,I'}$ be the map formed by the faces $\{\widetilde\mathfrak{tr}^{\mathrm{disk},n}(t):t\in I'\}\backslash\{\widetilde\mathfrak{tr}^{\mathrm{disk},n}(t_\varepsilon^-)\}$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:A2},  the interval $I'$ and the triangulation $T_{n,I'}$  here agrees with the interval $I'$ and the disk triangulation $T_{n,I'}$ in Definition~\ref{def:CPtoMOT} defined for the interval $I_{a,b}=[A\varepsilon,A(1-\varepsilon)]$ and $I=[A\varepsilon_1,A(1-\varepsilon_1)]$, and the triangulation $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T_{n,I'})$  is a submap of the triangulation $\Phi_{\rm simple}(\widetilde T^{\mathrm{disk},n})$.     Consider the path $\widetilde\gamma_{n,I'}$ on $\partial T_{n,I'}$ formed by the vertices $\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_1,...,\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_k$, such that $\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_1$ and $\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_k$ are also on the boundary of $\widetilde T^{\mathrm{disk},n}$ while the vertices on  $\partial T_{n,I'}$ other than $\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_2,...,\widetilde\mathfrak{v}_{k-1}$ are all on the boundary of $\widetilde T^{\mathrm{disk},n}$. Furthermore,

This along with the continuity of $\eta^\mathrm{disk}$ gives claim (ii).  For    claim (iii), by part (\ref{cond:lem:disk-pf-0-(v)}) of Lemma~\ref{lem:disk-pf-0}, if we send $n\to\infty$ then $\delta\to0$,  $$\max\Big\{\sup_{t\in[0,A\delta]}|n^{-1/2}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_t -1 |,    \sup_{t\in[0,A\delta]}|n^{-1/2}\widetilde\mathcal{R}_t|,  \sup_{t\in[A(1-\delta),A]}|n^{-1/2}\widetilde\mathcal{L}_t| , \sup_{t\in[A(1-\delta),A]}|n^{-1/2}\widetilde\mathcal{R}_t|\Big\} \to 0 \text{ in probability}, $$

label: eq:pf-417-1
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(\mathcal{X}_j,\mathcal{Y}_j)_{j\geq0}$ be a standard simple random random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and write $$q_m(x,y) = \mathbb{P}\big[(\mathcal{X}_m,\mathcal{Y}_m) = y, \mathcal{X}_j,\mathcal{Y}_j\geq 0\text{ for }j=0,...,m\big|(\mathcal{X}_0,\mathcal{Y}_0)=x\big].$$
    For the walk $(\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_t})_{0\leq t\leq 1}$, consider the event $E_n$ that $\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_0}=\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_1} = 0$, $\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_t}\in[0,\infty)^2$ for $t\in [0,1]$ and there are $2n$ jumps in total.  Let $p_\lambda(j) = \frac{\lambda^j}{j!}e^{-\lambda}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-excursion}, we have $\mathbb{P}[E_n]=p_{2n}(2n)q_{2n}(0,0) = p_{2n}(2n)4^{-2n}\#\mathcal{A}_n^\mathrm{sp} = c(1+o_n(1))n^{-7/2}$. Then conditioned on $E_n$,  $(\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_t})_{0\leq t\leq 1}$  has the same law as $(\widetilde\mathcal{Z}^n_t)_{t\in [0,1]}$. Then for any trace $w:[0,1-b-a]\to \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $w(1-b-a)=y\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $r$ jumps, the Radon-Nikodym derivative $X_{a,b}$ between the laws of  $(\widetilde\mathcal{Z}^n_{t+a}-\widetilde\mathcal{Z}^n_a)_{0\leq t\leq 1-b-a}$ and the unconditional law of  $(\check{\mathcal{Z}^n_t})_{0\leq t\leq 1-b-a}$ is
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pf-417-1}
        X_{a,b}(w) = \frac{1}{p_{2n}(2n)q_{2n}(0,0)}\Big(\sum_{ i+j = 2n-r} p_{2na}(i)p_{2nb}(j) \cdot\big(\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}q_i(0,x)q_j(x+y,0)\mathds{1}_{w(t)+x\in[0,\infty)^2 \forall t\in [0,1-a-b]} \big)\Big).
    \end{equation}
    We have $\sum_{ i+j = 2n-r} p_{2na}(i)p_{2nb}(j) = p_{2n(a+b)}(2n-r)\leq c_{a,b}n^{-1/2}$.
    By Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, 
    $$ \Big(\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}q_i(0,x)q_j(x+y,0)\Big)^2\leq \Big(\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}q_i(0,x)^2\Big)\Big(\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}q_j(x+y,0)^2\Big) = q_{2i}(0,0)q_{2j}(0,0).$$
    We have $p_{2an}(i)\leq c e^{-c'n}$ if $i<an$ and $p_{2bn}(j)\leq c e^{-c'n}$ if $j<bn$   for some constant $c>0$. For $i\geq an$ and $j\geq bn$, we have $q_{2i}(0,0)q_{2j}(0,0)\leq cn^{-6}$. Therefore the Radon-Nikodym derivative $X_{a,b}(w)$ is bounded from above by some constant $c$ depending only on $a,b$. This finishes the proof.

body_md:
\label{lem:pf-pack-cone-1}
    Let  $T$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:pack-cone}. Then $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is a.s.\ not empty. The simple random walk on $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is a.s.\ recurrent, and $T$ is circle packing parabolic.

title: Proof
body_md:
The first claim is a consequence of the Mullin bijection description of $T$ along with Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-excursion} and Proposition~\ref{lem:gap-hat-J-Q} and the Borel-Contelli lemma.   Let $  T^n$ be a disk triangulation defined as follows. Let  $\Phi_\mathrm{T}(\mathcal{Z}|_{[-n,n]}) = (  T^n, \widehat{\mathfrak{tr}}^n)$. We uniformly randomly pick a face of $ T^n$, and we uniformly randomly pick a vertex $ {v}^n$ on this face and  declare that $ {v}^n$ is the root of $\widehat T^n$.                                                                
  We also uniformly randomly pick a vertex $v$ on the face $\mathfrak{tr}(0)$ of $T$.  By~\cite[Lemma 3.3]{GRRiemann}, the rooted disk triangulations $(  T^n, v^n)$ converges in distribution to $(T,v)$ in Benjamini-Schramm topology, and by~\cite[Lemma 3.4]{GRRiemann}, $\mathbb{P}[\deg(v^n)\geq M]\leq 2(3/4)^{M/4}$ for $M\in\mathbb{N}$ for every $n$. Now independently for each multiple edge $(e_1,...,e_k)$ connecting to vertices $v_1$ and $v_2$ on $ T^n$, we further uniformly randomly keep one of these edges and remove the remaining $k-1$ of those, which further turns $ T^n$ to a simple graph $\widehat G^n$. Let $\widehat{G}$ be the simple graph generated by $T$ in the same way. Then the convergence above of $(\widehat G^n,\widehat v^n)$ to $(\widehat G,v)$ continues to hold, and $\mathbb{P}[\deg(v)\geq M]\leq 2(3/4)^{M/4}$ on $\widehat G$ since $\widehat{G}$ is obtained by removing only edges but not vertices from $T$. For a vertex $v_0$ of $T^n$, let $d(v_0)$ be its degree in $\widehat G^n$ and $f(v_0)$ be the number of faces in $T^n$ incident to $v_0$ (excluding the outer face). Then Lemma~\ref{lem:Euler} implies that $f(v_0)\leq 2d(v_0)$. On the other hand, each triangular face of $T^n$ incident to $v_0$ uses two edges incident to $v_0$, and therefore $d(v_0)\leq 2f(v_0)$. This further implies that, if we sample a vertex $\check{v}^n$ on $\widehat G^n$ with probability proportional to its degree, then the law of  $(\widehat G^n,\widehat v^n)$ and $(\widehat G^n,\check v^n)$ are mutually absolutely continuous with Radon-Nikodym derivative in $[1/4,4]$. Furthermore, the law of $(\widehat G^n,\check v^n)$ is tight and  any subsequential limiting rooted graph continues to have exponential tail for the degree of the root vertex, and its law is absolutely continuous with respect to $(\widehat G,v)$ with Radon-Nikodym derivative in $[1/4,4]$. 
  Now~\cite[Theorem 1.1]{GNrecurrence} implies that the simple random walk on $\widehat G$ is a.s.\ recurrent, and since $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ can be viewed as a subgraph of $\widehat G$, the simple  random walk on $\Phi_{\rm simple}(T)$ is a.s.\ recurrent. The last claim follows from~\cite[Theorem 1.1]{HeSchramm-hy-pa}.

body_md:
We proceed as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:cZ^n-pack-E}. Fix   $(a_n,b_n)\in K$ such that $(a_n,b_n)\to (a,b)$. Let $I' = I_{a,b}$ and $I_n' = I_{a_n,b_n}$ be the interval defined in Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT} for $I = I(0)$. Below we verify the convergence in Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT} with $I'_n$ in place of $I'$.  Let $t_{\rm mid}$ be the midpoint of $I'$,   $(T_{n,I_n'},\mathfrak{tr}_{n,I_n'}) = \Phi_\mathrm{T}(\mathcal{Z}^n|_{I_n' })$, and $\Phi_\mathrm{M}(\mathcal{Z}^n) = (M^n,e_0^n,\mathfrak{T}^n)$. Let $M_{n,I_n'}$, $t_{n,\rm mid}$, $\mathfrak{v}_{I_n'}^{\mathrm{mid},n}$ and $\widehat M_{n,I_n'}$ be defined as above Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT} for  $\mathcal{Z}^n|_{I_n'}$.                                                                                                                                 
    For $t\in \mathcal{J}_\mathrm{L}^{n,-}$, we also view $\mathfrak{v}_t^n$ as a point for the corresponding vertex on $\mathfrak{M}(M^n)$. For $t\in \mathcal{J}_\mathrm{R}^{n,-}$, we write $\mathfrak{f}_t^n$ for the face on $\mathfrak{M}(M^n)$ corresponding to the time $t$, and write $\mathfrak{v}_t^n$ for the center of the face  $\mathfrak{f}_t^n$  on $\mathfrak{M}(M^n)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:def-cZ^n} and Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-unif-Hcell} applied to $r = \mathrm{diam}(\eta^n([-2^{n+1},2^{n+1}])) = \mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}^{-1}\mathrm{diam}(\eta([-2,2]))$, as we scale by  $\mathfrak{R}_{2^{-n}}$, there is a conformal map  $\varphi^n:\mathfrak{M}(M^n)\to \mathbb{C}$ such that   in probability as $n\to\infty$,
    \begin{align}
    & \lim_{n\to\infty}  \sup\{|\eta(t) - \varphi^n(\mathfrak{v}_t^n) |: t\in \mathcal{J}_\mathrm{L}^{n,-},t\in [-2,2]\} = 0;  \label{eq:E-unif-0-0}  \\
 &  \lim_{n\to\infty} \sup\big\{ \mathrm{diam}(\varphi^n(\mathfrak{f}_t^n) ):  \mathfrak{f}_t^n \text{ is equal  or adjacent to a face  } \mathfrak{f}_s^n \text{ with } s\in [-2,2]\cap \mathcal{J}_\mathrm{R}^{n,-}\big\} = 0;  \label{eq:E-unif-0-1}  \\ & 
   \lim_{n\to\infty}  \sup\{ |\eta(t)-{\mathfrak{tr}^n}(t)|: t\in [-2,2]\} = 0.  \label{eq:E-unif-0-2}
\end{align}
where the convergence~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-2} is uniform over all choices of the path ${\mathfrak{tr}^n}$ on faces of $M^n$.

Using the scaling in Lemma~\ref{lem:def-cZ^n}, Proposition~\ref{prop:Tutte5.8} and  \cite[Lemma 5.36]{Tutte},  $t_{n,\rm mid}\to t_{\rm mid}$ in probability. By the independence between the dyadic system $\mathfrak{D}$ and $\eta$, almost surely, $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ is in the interior of $\eta(I')$. By the second part of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-unif-Hcell} and~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-1}, the curve distance~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0} between $\partial T_{n,I_n'}$ under the embedding $\varphi^n$ and $\partial\eta(I_n')$ tends to 0 in probability as $n\to\infty$. Using $(a_n,b_n)\to (a,b)$,   the two components of $(\eta(I_n')\backslash\eta(I'))\cup(\eta(I')\backslash\eta(I'_n))$ stays in a small neighborhood of starting and ending points of $\eta(I')$ in probability, respectively. In particular, the curve distance~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0} between $\partial\eta(I_n')$ and $\partial\eta(I')$ converges to 0 in probability.  Therefore~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-0} and~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-1}  further imply that with probability tending to 1 as $n\to\infty$, the vertex for $t_{n,\rm mid}$ in $M^n$ is on $T_{n,I_n'}$ and has at least graph distance 3 from the boundary of $T_{n,I_n'}$ and thus an interior vertex of the map $M_{n,I_n'}$. This verifies Condition~\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(i)} of Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT}.

For each   edge $e$ on the right boundary of $T_{n,I_n'}$, we associate it with the vertex $v_{e,\mathrm{L}}$ on $M_{n,I_n'}$ which is on the same triangular face of $T_{n,I_n'}$ with $e$. Then $v_{e,\mathrm{L}}$ is also on the boundary of $M_{n,I_n'}$.  For two clockwise consecutive edges $e_1,e_2$ on the right boundary of $T_{n,I_n'}$ sharing a common vertex $v$, the clockwise boundary arc of $\partial M_{n,I_n'}$ between $v_{e_1,\mathrm{L}}$ and $v_{e_2,\mathrm{L}}$ is contained within the single face on $M^n$ whose vertex on $T^n$ is $v$. Thus~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-1} and the second part of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-unif-Hcell} imply that when viewed as a loop that may traverse some edges for twice, $\partial \varphi^n( M_{n,I_n'})$ converges to $\partial\eta(I_n')$ and therefore $\partial\eta(I')$ in probability as $n\to\infty$ under the curve metric~\eqref{eq:curve-metric-0}. Furthermore, (the closure of) each connected component of $\partial \varphi^n(M_{n,I_n'})\backslash \partial \varphi^n(\widehat M_{n,I_n'})$, when viewed as a closed loop, has winding number 0 around $\varphi^n(\mathfrak{v}_{I'_n}^{\mathrm{mid},n})$, and $\varphi^n(\mathfrak{v}_{I_n'}^{\mathrm{mid},n})\to \eta(t_{\rm mid})$ in probability as $n\to\infty$. This gives Condition~\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(v)}.  Let $\tau^n(z) = z- \varphi^n(\mathfrak{v}_{I_n'}^{\mathrm{mid},n})+\eta(t_{\rm mid})$.                                                               
By Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-perturb}, up to a rotation, the conformal map $\widehat\varphi_{n,I_n'}:  \big(\tau^n\circ \varphi^n(\widehat M_{n,I_n'}) \big)\to\mathbb{D}$ sending $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ to 0 converges uniformly to the conformal map $\widehat\varphi: \eta(I' )\to \mathbb{D}$ sending $\eta(t_{\rm mid})$ to 0 in probability. Then using $\widehat t_{I_n'}^{n,\min}\to t_{I_n'}^-$, the distance between $\widehat\varphi_{n,I_n'}(\check\mathfrak{tr}_{n,I_n'}(\widehat t_{I_n'}^{n,\min}))$ and 1 tends to 0 in probability as $n\to\infty$, and the convergence of the conformal map  $\widehat\varphi_{n,I_n'}$ remains true if we further rotate such that the vertex $\check\mathfrak{tr}_{n,I_n'}(\widehat t_{I_n'}^{n,\min})$ is embedded at 1. Conditions~\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(ii)}-\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(iii)} in Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT} then follow by~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-1} and~\eqref{eq:E-unif-0-2}   where we  take $\varphi_{n,I_n'} =  \widehat\varphi_{n,I_n'}\circ \tau^n\circ\varphi^n$. Condition~\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(iv)} follows from the second part of Theorem~\ref{thm:conv-0-cone-unif-Hcell}, where by Condition~\ref{cond:def:uniftoMOT-(v)}, the number of edges  that is on the left boundary of $T_{n,I_n'}$ but not on the boundary of $\widehat M_{n,I_n'}$ divided by $2^{n/2}$ tends to 0 in probability as $n\to\infty$. This gives~\eqref{eq:q-q-prop:cZ^n-unif-E}, which further implies the desired convergence of Riemann uniformization to mating of trees by setting $(a_n,b_n)= (a,b)$.

By an identical proof, Lemma~\ref{lem:disk-pf-3} also holds for the sets of times encoding vertices or faces of $\mathfrak{M}(\widetilde M^{\mathrm{disk},n})$, i.e., we can replace the random times encoding the map $\widetilde M^{\mathrm{disk},n}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:disk-unif-pf-1} with equally spaced times. Therefore Theorem~\ref{thm:unif-disk} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:disk-unif-pf-1} by a further reparameterization as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:pack-disk}.

title: Lemma
body_md: Let $(\mathcal{Z}_k)_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a standard nearest-neighbor walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $\Phi_\mathrm{M}(\mathcal{Z}) = (M,e_0,\mathfrak{T})$. Then the Riemann surface $\mathfrak{M}(M)$ is a.s.\ parabolic.

title: Proof
body_md:
It is shown in~\cite{Che17} that $M$ is ergodic, recurrent and can be written as the Benjamini-Schramm limit of uniformly rooted planar maps where the root is chosen proportionally to its degree. Let $\rho$ be the root vertex defined in this way and let $\mathbb{P}$ be the law of $(M,\rho)$, which is reversible in the sense of~\cite[Section 2.3]{AHNR18unimodular}/ We write $\mathbb{P}_*$ for the law of $(M,\rho)$ weighted by $\deg(\rho)^{-1}/\mathbb{E}[\deg(\rho)^{-1}]$. Then $\mathbb{E}_*[\deg(\rho)] = 1/\mathbb{E}[\deg(\rho)^{-1}]<\infty$ and $(M,\rho)$ is unimodular under $\mathbb{P}_*$ as in~\cite[Proposition 2.3]{AHNR18unimodular}.
                                                                              
    The same continues to hold if we remove all the faces of $M$ with degree 1 or 2 as in the definition of $\mathfrak{M}(M)$. The claim then follows from~\cite[Theorem 1.1, (5)$\to$(9)]{AHNR18unimodular}.

    Let $(\widetilde \mathcal{Z}^n_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ be a rate $n$ continuous-time nearest-neighbor walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $\widetilde \mathcal{Z}^n_0=0$. Then there is a coupling for $(Z,(\widetilde\mathcal{Z}^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}})$ such that Assertions \ref{result:thm:unif-cone-1}-\ref{result:thm:unif-cone-3}\ in Theorem~\ref{thm:unif-cone} holds for $\widetilde\mathcal{Z}^n$ instead of $\mathcal{Z}^n$. Furthermore, for each $R>0$, with probability tending to 1 as $n\to\infty$ then $K\to\infty$,  there does not exist any time $t\in \mathcal{J}^{n,-}_\mathrm{L}$ such that $|t|\geq K$ while the vertex for the time $t$ is embedded inside $B(0;R)$, and  there does not exist any time $t\in \mathcal{J}^{n,-}_\mathrm{R}$ such that $|t|\geq K$ while the face for the time $t$ intersects $B(0;R)$ under the embedding $\varphi^n$.

title: Proof

Then the conclusions as in Definition~\ref{def:uniftoMOT} still hold if we assume that $\varphi_{jn,I}(\mathfrak{v}^{n,j,0})=0$.
